Here is how we will import our data: 

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DATA = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LucyMcGowan/sta-363-f26/main/data/"
Auto = pd.read_csv(DATA + "Auto.csv")
```

## R to Python

| Task | R | Python |
|---|---|---|
| read a csv | `read_csv("f.csv")` | `pd.read_csv("f.csv")` |
| first rows | `head(d)` | `d.head()` |
| dimensions | `dim(d)` | `d.shape` |
| column names | `names(d)` | `d.columns` |
| one column | `d$mpg` | `d["mpg"]` |
| several columns | `d[, c("mpg", "weight")]` | `d[["mpg", "weight"]]` |
| filter rows | `d[d$mpg > 30, ]` | `d[d["mpg"] > 30]` |
| new column | `d$kpl <- d$mpg * 0.425` | `d["kpl"] = d["mpg"] * 0.425` |
| summary | `summary(d)` | `d.describe()` |
| counts | `table(d$origin)` | `d["origin"].value_counts()` |
| mean | `mean(d$mpg)` | `d["mpg"].mean()` |
| group means | `aggregate(mpg ~ origin, d, mean)` | `d.groupby("origin")["mpg"].mean()` |
| sequence | `1:10` | `range(1, 11)` |
| length | `length(x)` | `len(x)` |
| missing | `is.na(x)` | `x.isna()` |

Python counts from **zero**, so `d.iloc[0]`
is the first row. And `range(1, 11)` **excludes** the endpoint, so it stops at
10.

## Selecting

```{python}
Auto[["mpg", "horsepower", "weight"]].head(3)
```

```{python}
Auto[Auto["mpg"] > 40][["name", "mpg"]]
```

If you have multiple conditions, you use `&` for and, `|` for or, and parentheses around each piece:

```{python}
Auto[(Auto["mpg"] > 30) & (Auto["year"] > 78)].shape
```

## Model fitting


```{python}
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

X = Auto[["horsepower", "weight"]]   # predictors, always a data frame
y = Auto["mpg"]                      # response, always a single column

model = LinearRegression()           # 1. choose
model.fit(X, y)                      # 2. fit
model.predict(X.head(3))             # 3. predict
```

```{python}
model.score(X, y)                    # 4. score
```

Swap `LinearRegression()` for `KNeighborsRegressor(5)` or
`RandomForestRegressor()` and the other three lines stay as they are. 

## Pipelines

A pipeline attaches preprocessing to a model so they always occur together.

```{python}
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsRegressor
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline

pipe = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), KNeighborsRegressor(10))
pipe.fit(X, y)
pipe.score(X, y)
```

## Plotting

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))
ax.scatter(Auto["horsepower"], Auto["mpg"], s=12, alpha=0.6, color="#d5008f")
ax.set_xlabel("horsepower")
ax.set_ylabel("mpg")
plt.show()
```


## Errors you may see

**`NameError: name 'X' is not defined`**
You did not run the cell that created `X`, or the runtime restarted. Run your cells from the top.

**`KeyError: 'mpg'`**
That column does not exist. Check `Auto.columns` for the exact spelling. Column names are case sensitive.

**`ValueError: Expected 2D array, got 1D array instead`**
scikit-learn wants predictors as a data frame. Use `Auto[["horsepower"]]` with
two sets of brackets, not `Auto["horsepower"]`.

**`SettingWithCopyWarning`**
You modified a slice of a data frame. Add `.copy()` when you subset something you
intend to change.

More in [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd).
